preview_text: Edin Džeko starts R3 after being subbed off in the 64th minute against Switzerland in R2 — Bosnia lost 4-1 with only Ermin Mahmić scoring a 90th-minute consolation. Mahmić now starts as a forward alongside Džeko and carries the goal scorer upside from that late strike.

Nikola Vasilj made 11 saves against Switzerland — an extraordinary individual performance in a losing effort. Corner kicks are taken by Kerim Alajbegovic, Esmir Bajraktarevic, and Ivan Bašić. Bosnia need a win against Qatar to keep advancement hopes alive, which elevates their attacking ceiling in this game.

Bosnia were outshot 15-7 on target in R2 against Switzerland, conceding four second-half goals including a brace from Johan Manzambi off the bench and a Ruben Vargas strike. Sead Kolašinac and Nikola Katić start at center back. Amar Dedić received a yellow card in the 59th minute in R2 and returns at right back.

Džeko leads Bosnia in projection but his R2 sub timing at 64 minutes introduces floor risk. Mahmić is the GPP leverage play — he scored in R2 and starts at a cheaper salary. Alajbegovic handles corners and provides set piece upside. Bosnia are heavy favorites against Qatar and a multi-goal win opens up multiple scorers.

Qatar were hammered 6-0 by Canada in R2 — Jonathan David scored three, Cyle Larin and Nathan Saliba added goals, and Mohamed Manai put through his own net. Mahmoud Abunada starts in goal against Bosnia despite the concessions. Akram Afif leads the Qatar attack and takes corners.

Boualem Khoukhi scored Qatar's goal in R1 against Switzerland and starts at center back in R3. Edmilson Junior starts at forward alongside Afif. Qatar are eliminated from advancement contention entering this game; the lineup saw multiple changes after the 0-6 result with several R2 starters absent.

Qatar generated 5 shots in R2 against Canada and gave up 22. Abunada faced 15 shots on target in that match. In R1 against Switzerland, Qatar drew 1-1 with Khoukhi equalizing in the 90th minute. Yusuf Abdurisag starts as the striker and is Qatar's only player who can generate GPP upside in a must-win situation for Bosnia.

Qatar players carry elimination game risk and low implied probability. Afif at corner kick taker is the only play worth rostering — his set piece volume and attacking role make him the lone GPP option. Abunada has GK save upside if Bosnia pile on shots. Otherwise, QAT is a fade game.

Matheus Cunha scored twice in R2 against Haiti — 23rd and 36th minutes, the second assisted by Vinicius Júnior — and was subbed off in the 64th minute for Endrick. Cunha returns to the starting lineup and leads Brazil in R3 projection alongside Vinicius Júnior, who assisted Cunha's second goal and scored the third himself in the 45th minute.

Vinicius Júnior is the highest-projected player on the entire slate at $19.36 fpts. Lucas Paquetá assisted Vinicius's 45th-minute goal against Haiti and starts in attacking midfield. Rayan starts at right forward after replacing Raphinha in the 40th minute in R2 — Raphinha does not appear in the R3 starting XI.

Brazil won 3-0 against Haiti in R2, their second consecutive win. Alisson faced 4 shots on target and made 0 saves. Bruno Guimarães and Matheus Cunha handle corners. Casemiro starts in defensive midfield. Gabriel Magalhães and Marquinhos return at center back. Brazil are through to the knockouts entering R3.

Vinicius-Cunha is the primary Brazil stack — both scored or assisted in R2 and have the highest projection pairing on the slate. Lucas Paquetá is the third stack option via assists. Rayan at forward is a lower-owned ceiling play if Brazil scores multiple. Alisson carries GK upside only if Scotland generates shots.

Scotland lost 0-1 to Morocco in R2 — Ismael Saibari scored in the 2nd minute from a Brahim Díaz assist, and Scotland never equalized despite 8 shots on target. Angus Gunn made 5 saves in R2. John McGinn was replaced in the 89th minute by Ross Stewart; McGinn returns to start R3 and handles corner kicks.

Scotland need a result against Brazil to clinch advancement from Group C. Ryan Christie and Lewis Ferguson also take corners. Ben Gannon-Doak entered at the 60th minute in R2 for Kieran Tierney and now appears in the starting XI alongside McTominay. Ché Adams starts as the lone striker.

Scotland are 3 points through two games — a win or draw against Brazil could advance them. In R2 against Morocco they had 3 shots on target vs Morocco's 6. Andy Robertson played the full 90 in R2 before taking a knock (65'). Nathan Patterson and Gannon-Doak provide width. Scott McTominay leads box-to-box volume from midfield.

Scotland players are heavy underdogs against Brazil with low implied probability. McGinn via corners is the only floor-driven play. Gunn has save-based GPP upside if Brazil generate the volume they showed against Haiti. Adams as a striker is a low-ownership tournament punt. Otherwise SCO is a chalky fade in GPP.

Jonathan David scored a hat-trick against Qatar in R2 — 29th, 45th, and 90th minutes, the last assisted by Nathan Saliba. David returns as the primary striker and leads Canada in attacking projection. Cyle Larin also scored in R2 in the 16th minute and starts alongside David.

Nathan Saliba scored in the 64th minute in R2 and assisted David's 90th-minute goal — he starts in central midfield and carries dual offensive value. Stephen Eustaquio and Ali Ahmed handle corner kicks. Maxime Crépeaux kept a clean sheet against Qatar and is the top DFS goalkeeper on this slate.

Canada demolished Qatar 6-0 in R2, their best result of the tournament. The game total vs Switzerland is 2.61 — much tighter than the Qatar matchup. Canada and Switzerland are level on points entering R3 with the winner likely topping Group B. Richie Laryea and Alistair Johnston play full-back on either side.

David-Larin is the Canadian stack but this is a genuine contest vs Switzerland — the 6-0 game was a blowout vs an eliminated Qatar side and doesn't translate directly. Saliba is a low-ownership mid stack play. Crépeaux is a high-floor GK in a game with a 2.61 total. Eustaquio via corners provides floor upside.

Johan Manzambi came on in the 71st minute against Bosnia and scored twice — 74th and 90th minutes — as Switzerland won 4-1 in R2. He now starts for the first time in R3. Ruben Vargas also entered at 71 minutes in R2, scored at 84 minutes with an assist from Breel Embolo, and returns to the starting lineup.

Breel Embolo starts as the central striker and recorded the assist on Vargas's R2 goal. Granit Xhaka scored a 90th-minute penalty against Bosnia. Dan Ndoye was subbed off in the 71st minute in R2 but returns to the starting XI alongside Manzambi and Vargas. Ruben Vargas and Ricardo Rodríguez take corner kicks.

Switzerland won 4-1 against Bosnia with three second-half goals from substitutes. Gregor Kobel made 4 saves in R2. Against Qatar in R1, Switzerland drew 1-1 — Embolo scored the penalty but Khoukhi equalized in the 90th minute. Switzerland are level with Canada in Group B; this is effectively a knockout game.

Manzambi is the highest-leverage SUI play — his R2 brace as a sub elevated his projection but he is still lower-owned than the established names. Vargas-Embolo is the stack; both contributed to R2 goals. Kobel has clean sheet upside in a defensive matchup with Canada. Xhaka via penalty upside rounds out the SUI options.

Michal Sadílek scored in the 6th minute against South Africa in R2 with an assist from Alexandr Sojka. Sadílek returns in central midfield and is one of the few CZE players with a verified R2 goal. Patrik Schick does not appear in the R3 starting XI — Pavel Šulc and Adam Hložek lead the forward line.

Czechia drew 1-1 with South Africa in R2 — Teboho Mokoena equalized from the penalty spot after Sadílek's early lead. Vladimir Coufal starts at right back and takes corner kicks. Ladislav Krejčí took a yellow card in R2 and returns at center back. David Doudera starts alongside Coufal in a midfield role.

Czechia are in a difficult position entering R3 — they need a win against Mexico and other results to advance. Matej Kovár starts in goal. Denis Višinský and Šulc start as forwards, with Hložek behind. Lukáš Červ starts in a defensive midfield role. Czechia had 5 shots on target vs RSA, conceding the equalizer from a penalty.

Sadílek is the only verified CZE goalscorer in this tournament and is the primary offensive midfield target. Šulc and Hložek are the striker options in a long-shot advancement scenario. Coufal handles corners and provides set piece upside. Against a Mexico side already qualified, CZE carry risk of a conservative opponent.

Luis Romo scored Mexico's only goal in R2 against Korea Republic — a 50th-minute strike that sealed a 1-0 win. Romo returns in central midfield. Raúl Jiménez leads the attack as striker. Roberto Alvarado handles corner kicks from a wide midfield role and leads Mexico in R3 projection.

Mexico have already qualified for the knockouts with two wins in Group A. Julián Quiñones starts as a winger. Edson Álvarez anchors defensive midfield. Raúl Rangel starts in goal — he faced 2 shots on target and made 1 save against Korea Republic. Mateo Chávez and César Montes start at center back.

Mexico's 1-0 win over Korea Republic in R2 came from a Romo goal in the 50th minute, with Mexico shutting Korea out despite Son Heung-min being available. Rangel's GK projection of $7.37 fpts is high for this slate — clean sheet upside drives that. Mexico have the highest implied probability of any team in the CZE_MEX game.

Alvarado via corners is the floor-driven MEX play. Jiménez is the striker with goal scorer upside against Czechia's porous defense (gave up a penalty in R2). Romo is the cheapest verified goal scorer on the MEX side but carries limited upside at his salary. Rangel is a sneaky GK value if Mexico keep a clean sheet.

Haiti lost 0-3 to Brazil in R2 — Matheus Cunha scored twice and Vinicius Júnior added a third before halftime. Johny Placide made 5 saves in that match and returns in goal. Frantzdy Pierrot and Wilson Isidor start as forwards against Morocco in R3.

Jean-Ricner Bellegarde leads Haiti in projection and takes corner kicks. Ruben Providence also takes corners. Carlens Arcus starts at right back after receiving a yellow card in the 4th minute of R2. Haiti are eliminated entering R3 and need a result purely for pride — Morocco are a heavy favorite.

Haiti have been outscored 4-0 across two matches. They generated 4 shots on target against Brazil with Placide facing 7 SOT and conceding 3. In R1 against Scotland they lost 0-1. Martin Expérience starts at left center back. Louicius Deedson and Danley Jean-Jacques start in midfield.

Haiti are 80% underdogs against Morocco with a low implied score. Placide via saves is the only floor-driven play. Pierrot and Isidor are long-shot GPP darts at low ownership. In a slate with better options, Haiti players are typically used only for salary relief.

Ismael Saibari scored in the 2nd minute against Scotland in R2, assisted by Brahim Díaz — the goal stood as the match-winner in a 1-0 result. Saibari starts again as the primary striker and leads Morocco in DFS projection at $16.12 fpts. Brahim Díaz was replaced in the 84th minute in R2 but returns to start R3.

Achraf Hakimi leads Morocco in fpts at $16.60 and handles corner kicks alongside Bilal El Khannouss. Yassine Bounou made 7 saves against Scotland — Morocco conceded 8 shots on target while keeping the 1-0 lead. Azzedine Ounahi and Neil El Aynaoui round out the midfield. Morocco are level on points with Brazil entering R3.

Morocco are through to the knockouts alongside Brazil in Group C. Their R2 win over Scotland came from a very early Saibari goal — Brahim Díaz registered the assist and was subbed off late. Noussair Mazraoui starts at left back. Chadi Riad and Issa Diop start at center back. Ayyoub Bouaddi starts in holding midfield.

Saibari-Brahim Díaz is the Morocco stack — both contributed to the R2 winner. Hakimi via corners adds set piece upside to his already high projection. El Khannouss is a secondary corner taker worth considering. Bounou could accumulate DFS points if Haiti generate any shots. Morocco face the lowest-quality opponent on the slate.

Son Heung-Min was subbed off in the 57th minute against Mexico in R2 — Korea lost 1-0 to a Luis Romo goal. Son returns to the starting lineup in R3 against South Africa and handles corner kicks alongside Lee Kang-In. Lee Kang-In received a yellow card in the 4th minute of R2 and played the full match.

Korea need a win against South Africa to secure advancement. Hwang In-Beom starts in central midfield. Lee Jae-Sung starts at forward. Kim Seung-Gyu made 2 saves against Mexico. Paik Seung-Ho and Seol Young-Woo return in midfield. Korea had 2 shots on target in R2 — a flat attacking output they need to improve against RSA.

Korea are 3 points entering R3 after a draw and a loss. They beat Czechia 2-1 in R1 — both goals from second-half substitutes Hwang Hee-chan and Oh Hyeon-gyu. Lee Gi-Hyuk, Kim Min-Jae, and Lee Han-Beom form the back three. Kim Moon-Hwan starts at right midfield. Korea have a +0 goal difference entering the decisive game.

Son-Lee Kang-In is the Korean stack and the highest-projection pairing in this game. Both take corners and contribute to set pieces. Hwang In-Beom provides box-to-box assist upside. Kim Seung-Gyu is a mid-priced GK if Korea keep a clean sheet. This is a competitive game with advancement stakes on both sides.

Teboho Mokoena scored a penalty equalizer against Czechia in R2 after Michal Sadílek gave CZE the lead in the 6th minute. The 1-1 draw keeps South Africa in advancement contention entering R3. Mokoena does not appear in the R3 starting XI — Thapelo Maseko and Jayden Adams start in central midfield.

Oswin Appollis leads South Africa in projection at $9.63 fpts and takes corner kicks. Aubrey Modiba also takes corners from left back. Evidence Makgopa starts as the lone striker. Ronwen Williams starts in goal — he made 4 saves against Czechia. Thalente Mbatha starts in midfield after her R2 performance.

South Africa are 1 point through two games — a draw with Mexico in R1 and a draw with Czechia in R2. They need to beat Korea to have any chance of advancement. In R2 against Czechia, RSA generated 20 shots but only 7 on target with Williams coming from his own box. Mbekezeli Mbokazi and Ime Okon start at center back.

Appollis via corners is the primary RSA floor play. Makgopa is a low-ownership striker dart if RSA score an upset result. Williams has save-based upside against a Korea side that had limited attacking output in R2. RSA are underdogs here but the must-win scenario elevates their attacking intent and DFS ceiling.
